title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) to measure the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) on intent→configuration NetOps tasks when the identical initial generated candidate is deterministically reused by both conditions (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (model configuration records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Contingency counts: n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The exact two-sided McNemar p-value (exact binomial-tail convention) equals 1.0. A paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute risk difference with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729) equals [0.00, 0.015]. The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation in an extreme-difficulty task (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3). We report preregistration, complete execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostics for the repaired pair, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Motivation and scope. Translating operator intent into device configuration is a practical NetOps use case for large language models (LLMs). For operational acceptance, synthesized configurations must satisfy deterministic invariants (e.g., required sequencing of multi-device commands, allowed field updates, group-level availability constraints). Tool-mediated pipelines that validate and, where possible, repair generated artifacts before deployment are a proposed control to reduce incorrect changes, but it is not settled how much marginal benefit a bounded verifier-triggered repair provides when the same initial generated candidate is reused in both comparison conditions.

Estimand clarity. This study isolates the repair-only effect by enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics: each task produced exactly one sampled candidate, deterministically reused by the baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator may trigger ≤1 repair) episodes. Under these semantics any paired difference can arise only from the deterministic verifier and the single permitted repair. We therefore evaluate the estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (per-task binary acceptance difference) and explicitly do not claim evidence about independent guarded re-generation, multi-sample selection, or constrained prompting effects that would require independent first-pass draws.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifacted paired experiment (N=200 tasks) measuring a repair-only estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics with a deterministic verifier and gpt-5-mini. (2) Complete deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and exactly one repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Confirmatory paired analysis (n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0), risk difference = 0.005, exact McNemar p = 1.0, and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) Artifact-grounded diagnostic for the single repaired pair showing a required-sequence ordering breach repaired by the bounded remediation. (5) Reproducibility guidance and limitations tied to archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Synthesis of verified literature. Prior works show active prototype development and benchmarking for intent→config translation and LLM-augmented NetOps [1],[?]. Deterministic configuration verifiers have been developed to check syntactic and semantic invariants (reachability, ordering, group constraints) and serve as operational oracles for correctness evaluation [2]. In adjacent domains, generate→validate→repair patterns have been demonstrated (for example, program-repair workflows) and motivate verifier-aware pipelines here, but those demonstrations do not by themselves establish identical empirical effects in network-configuration contexts because network invariants and sequencing dependencies differ [4].

Tool-augmentation and agentic pipelines. Work on tool-augmented LLM agents and externally coupled solvers emphasizes integration challenges (interface design, oracle specification, provenance) and shows architectural promise for combining generators with specialized verifiers or repair engines [6]. Reporting- and preregistration-focused guidelines for LLM studies informed our preregistration and archival choices [3].

Limitations of prior empirical claims. The supplied verified records support proposals, demonstrations, and adjacent-domain empirical results, but they do not prove that guarded generate→validate→repair pipelines uniformly improve operational correctness in NetOps. Accordingly, our Related Work synthesizes prior findings as motivation and frames the present study narrowly: it evaluates a repair-only estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics using a deterministic synthetic task bank and a deterministic verifier; it does not claim broad production generality beyond those boundaries.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design. The study, preregistered as CAND-2026-001, fixed a paired binary estimand comparing per-task deterministic-verifier acceptance under baseline (no repair) versus guarded (verifier may trigger ≤1 repair) conditions, N=200 tasks, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, a maximum of one automated repair call per task, primary failed-call treatment complete_pair_primary, and confirmatory tests (exact two-sided McNemar plus paired-bootstrap percentile CI). The preregistration and all supporting artifacts are archived in the execution bundle.

Task generation and deterministic verifier. Tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and selected by a fixed index rule. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies. The verifier deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses generated commands, enforces allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, checks required_sequence ordering, evaluates group-level invariants (final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups), and returns full_intent_constraint_validation only when all encoded constraints are satisfied. Verifier tracer outputs are the authoritative scoring evidence; those traces are archived and form the basis for episode outcomes.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and sampling. The adapter contract deterministically reused exactly one initial generation per pair for both baseline and guarded conditions; no independent guarded first-pass generation was executed. The model-configuration record declares requested_model = gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling is a possible background property despite the enforced single-sample-per-pair design.

Sanitizer, repair policy, and provider accounting. A deterministic formatting sanitizer ran before verifier parsing. If the verifier found violations the guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call to the hosted model using a repair prompt constructed from the archived validator trace, as preregistered. Deterministic reconciliation and provider-call accounting record 200 shared_initial_generation calls and 1 repair call, summing to hosted_model_call_event_count = 201; cache_miss_count = 201, cache_hit_count = 0.

Statistical procedures and estimand interpretation. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar implemented via the exact binomial-tail formulation (p = 2 × min{BinomCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 − BinomCDF(k − 1; n, 0.5)}). With n = n10 + n01 and k = n10 the test evaluates the symmetry of discordant counts; under shared_initial_candidate semantics this discordance arises only from validator-triggered repair. Paired absolute risk difference used a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis executor and its seeds are archived so the reported contingency counts and CI reproduce from the raw results.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The execution manifest records start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00 (elapsed ≈29 minutes). planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}. These stage_counts are authoritative for total model-call accounting.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Baseline successes = 199 and failures = 1 (baseline success_rate = 0.995). Guarded successes = 200 and failures = 0 (guarded success_rate = 1.0). Contingency table: n11 = 199, n10 = 1 (guarded-only success), n01 = 0 (baseline-only success), n00 = 0. Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. With n = n10 + n01 = 1 and k = n10 = 1, the exact two-sided McNemar p-value (exact-binomial convention) equals p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) equals [0.00, 0.015]. These numeric outputs are archived and reproduce when the archived analysis executor is re-run on the raw results.

Single repair diagnostic. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair. Archived validator traces for that pair show a required_sequence ordering violation in the shared initial candidate; task difficulty metadata for that task recorded required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, difficulty.level = "extreme". The verifier trace presents validation_before.violation_codes identifying an ordering breach and validation_after.valid = true once the bounded repair was applied; the scorer returned score = 1 with scorer_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION". Those tracer fields constitute the archived evidence that the single observed paired improvement resulted from a verifier-triggered repair that enacted the required reordering.

Difficulty composition and exploratory diagnostics. Representative task manifests in the archive show required_command_count spanning 3–9 and changed_interface_count up to 3; tasks with larger required_command_count and higher changed_interface_count appear concentrated among the very_hard and extreme difficulty strata. The lone baseline failure and the single repaired pair are associated with extreme composite difficulty patterns in the archived metadata, consistent with the preregistered exploratory hypothesis that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity concentrate residual failures.

Missingness, exclusions, and reconciliation. No preregistered exclusions occurred and no persistent unparsables were recorded; missingness summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zeros on other categories. Deterministic reconciliation indicates pair_accounting_consistent = true and all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true.
sections.discussion:
What the paired estimand measures. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the experiment isolates the marginal effect of permitting a validator-triggered bounded repair on an identical initial candidate. This estimand answers a precise operational question: given a single sampled generated candidate, does permitting one verifier-driven repair meaningfully increase the chance that the deterministic verifier accepts the final configuration? It does not estimate benefits that could arise from independent guarded first-pass re-generation, multi-sample selection, constrained prompts, or repeated multi-step repair.

Interpretation in a sparse-discordant regime. The observed contingency (one discordant pair in favor of guarded) places the confirmatory test in a sparse-discordant regime. Exact McNemar p = 1.0 reflects limited directional evidence when discordant counts are minimal; the paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] quantifies an upper bound on plausible absolute improvement compatible with the observed data under the repair-only estimand. Practically, an observed baseline of 199/200 reduces inferential sensitivity for detecting small marginal improvements; the preregistered power plan targeted larger absolute increases (~10–15 percentage points) under mid-range baseline assumptions and therefore did not anticipate this high baseline ceiling.

Localized failure diagnosis and mechanism. The single repair-corrected case shows a concrete mechanism by which validator-guided bounded repair can help: the verifier detected a required_sequence ordering breach and the repair prompt, constructed deterministically from the verifier trace, resulted in a corrected command ordering that satisfied the encoded workflow policy. This artifact-grounded example demonstrates that when misconfigurations are expressible in the verifier’s manifest (ordering constraints, allowed field touch rules, group-level availability), a bounded automated repair can correct those faults for that class of errors.

Limitations and threats to validity. Internal validity: the paired shared_initial_candidate design intentionally isolates repair effects but does not address sampling variability or prompt sensitivity; the model-configuration record sets temperature = null/unset, which is explicitly not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but does not emulate vendor-specific runtime or dataplane behaviors; some real-world errors (e.g., vendor command idiosyncrasies, dataplane-only failures) are not captured. External validity: single-model study (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank constrain generality across models, datasets, and production topologies. Statistical limitation: with only one discordant pair, statistical power to detect small repair-only effects is limited; the bootstrap CI provides a bounded quantification of that uncertainty.

Operational implications (bounded). Artifact-grounded evidence supports a narrow conclusion: in this synthetic deterministic task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a verifier-triggered bounded repair corrected a localized multi-step ordering fault in one extreme task. This supports the design pattern that verifier-guided bounded repairs can remediate ordering/dependency violations that are specified in the verifier’s manifest. It is not evidence that bounded repair will correct errors observable only at dataplane runtime, nor that guarded repair will address adversarially poisoned contexts; those require live emulation, multi-model replication, and adversarial testing.

Concrete next validation steps (supported by artifacts as future work). The archived evidence suggests targeted follow-ups: (1) replicate the paired shared_initial_candidate estimand across multiple hosted models and varied model-control settings to characterize model-specific repair responsiveness; (2) evaluate independent-first-pass guarded semantics (independent guarded generation per arm) to estimate gains from guarded re-generation and sample selection; (3) integrate deterministic verification with dataplane emulation or vendor-specific execution (live-device or emulated dataplane) to assess beyond-manifest runtime behaviors; and (4) perform adversarial retrieval/poisoning experiments to quantify guarded-pipeline robustness under contaminated contexts. These steps are proposed as future validation axes, not as additional claims from the present run.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment that isolates the repair-only effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. In 200 deterministic synthetic intent→configuration tasks with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation (task-level difficulty: required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3). Paired absolute risk difference = 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. Artifact-grounded evidence therefore supports the constrained scientific conclusion that verifier-guarded bounded repair can correct localized ordering faults when those faults are expressible in the verifier’s encoded invariants. Broader operational claims require additional experiments (multi-model replication, independent-first-pass guarded semantics, adversarial contamination testing, and live-device/dataplane emulation).

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
